section_summary: This section covers State Department and SCAP records concerning public entertainment, theater, and the motion picture industry in occupied Japan from 1945 to 1949. Key subjects include the postwar resurgence of the Japanese leftist theater following the release of political prisoner Yoshi Hijikata, the distribution and exhibition of American films in Japan by the Motion Picture Export Association, and disputes regarding independent distributors seeking entry into the Japanese market. It also documents diplomatic interactions concerning the importation quota on Soviet films under Allied Council oversight, commercial inquiries regarding frozen yen assets and film production, and statistical data on Japanese cinema facilities.

subfiles.about: A telegram reporting German press accounts that 82 of 224 Tokyo cinemas were closed to conserve fuel and electricity.
subfiles.summary: Harrison reports German press accounts that 82 Tokyo cinemas closed February 1 to conserve electricity and coal.
subfiles.title: Closure of Tokyo Motion Picture Theaters for War Effort

subfiles.about: A cover despatch transmitting a memorandum of conversation with former political prisoner Yoshi Hijikata concerning Japan's progressive theater.
subfiles.from: Office of the United States Political Adviser, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmits a memorandum of conversation with released leftist theater leader Yoshi Hijikata concerning Japan's progressive theater prospects.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 36: Leftist Theater Movement in Japan

subfiles.about: A memorandum of conversation recording Yoshi Hijikata's account of his theatrical career, exile, imprisonment, and anticipated postwar theatrical resurgence.
subfiles.summary: Yoshi Hijikata discusses his theatrical career, foreign exile, and imprisonment, anticipating a postwar theatrical revival by 1947 under new democratic freedoms, and provides extensive lists of active Japanese playwrights, actors, and producers.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation on the Japanese Leftist Theater
subfiles.to: Office of the United States Political Adviser

subfiles.about: A letter proposing that the State Department send a representative to an Army-sponsored native goodwill carnival on Okinawa.
subfiles.summary: Hefter proposes State Department representation at an Army-sponsored native goodwill carnival on Okinawa scheduled for May 30, 1947.
subfiles.title: Letter Proposing State Department Participation in Okinawa Carnival
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: A letter acknowledging Hefter's suggestion and stating that the carnival program was forwarded to the Yokohama branch of the Political Adviser's office.
subfiles.summary: Allison acknowledges Hefter's letter and states that the carnival proposal was referred to the Political Adviser's Yokohama branch.
subfiles.title: Reply Concerning Proposed Attendance at Okinawa Carnival

subfiles.about: An instruction transmitting Hefter's letter and carnival program to Yokohama officials in case a staff visit coincides with the event.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Hefter's letter and carnival program to Yokohama officials in the event periodic visits coincide with the festivities.
subfiles.title: Instruction Transmitting Correspondence Concerning Okinawa Carnival
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, Yokohama Branch, Office of the United States Political Adviser

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet recording an MPPDA letter outlining the motion picture situation in Argentina, Brazil, and Japan.
subfiles.from: Motion Picture Producers & Distributors of America, Inc.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference sheet citing an MPPDA letter outlining motion picture conditions in Argentina, Brazil, and Japan.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference File Note: Motion Picture Situation in Argentina, Brazil, and Japan

subfiles.about: A letter requesting State Department assistance to determine the status of over two million yen held by MGM in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Loew's International requests State Department assistance in determining the status of over two million yen deposited in Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Inquiry Regarding Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Funds in Tokyo

subfiles.about: A letter advising Loew's to direct inquiries regarding its Tokyo yen balances to National City Bank's New York office.
subfiles.summary: Advises Loew's to address inquiries regarding Tokyo yen balances directly to National City Bank's New York office.
subfiles.title: Status of Loew's Yen Funds in Tokyo

subfiles.about: A military telegram reporting box-office grosses for American films shown in Tokyo, an amusement tax reduction, and nationwide bookings.
subfiles.summary: Reports Tokyo box-office success of two American films, nationwide theater bookings, and an amusement tax reduction to fifty percent.
subfiles.title: Box Office Report on American Motion Pictures in Tokyo

subfiles.about: A letter acknowledging State Department receipt and transmission of a Tokyo cable regarding the picture 'Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs'.
keywords: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges State Department information regarding a Tokyo cable concerning the film Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs.
subfiles.title: Acknowledgment Regarding Cable on 'Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs'

subfiles.about: An outgoing telegram directing that prints of 'Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs' be withheld from release in Tokyo pending an agreement with Disney.
keywords: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
subfiles.summary: Instructs Bergher in Tokyo to withhold Snow White prints because Disney has not yet signed an MPEA agreement.
subfiles.title: Instruction to Withhold Prints of 'Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs'
subfiles.to: Advance Echelon GHQ, Civil Information and Education Section, Tokyo

subfiles.about: A telegraphic request asking the State Department to transmit an urgent cable to Bergher in Tokyo to withhold 'Snow White' prints.
subfiles.summary: Requests urgent transmission of a cable instructing Bergher to withhold Snow White prints pending Disney's agreement with MPEA.
subfiles.title: Request to Transmit Cable Concerning 'Snow White' Prints to Tokyo

subfiles.about: A military telegram confirming that prints of 'Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs' have not been released in Tokyo and await instructions.
keywords: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
subfiles.summary: Tokyo military headquarters confirms prints of Snow White have been withheld pending further instructions from Mayer.
subfiles.title: Confirmation of Withholding Prints of 'Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs'

subfiles.about: A letter conveying a paraphrased Tokyo cable recommending that Mayer review film operations with CAD and OIC.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Tokyo recommendation that Mayer review film operations with CAD and OIC prior to discussions with firms.
subfiles.title: Transmission of Message Regarding Review of Tokyo Film Operations

subfiles.about: A cover letter transmitting Report Number 1 on Japanese Motion Picture Production for 1944-1945 to the Commerce Department.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Report Number 1 on Japanese motion picture production for 1944 to 1945 to the Commerce Department.
subfiles.title: Transmittal of Report on Japanese Motion Picture Production

subfiles.about: A Senate referral slip referring Transpacific Film Corporation correspondence to the Secretary of State.
subfiles.summary: Senate referral slip transmitting Transpacific Film Corporation correspondence to the Secretary of State.
subfiles.title: Senate Referral Slip Transmitting Transpacific Film Corporation Matter

subfiles.about: A letter transmitting an application to export independent American motion pictures to Japan and protesting MPEA's alleged monopoly.
subfiles.summary: Transpacific Film Corporation applies to export independent films to Japan and open an exchange, protesting the Motion Picture Export Association's alleged distribution monopoly.
subfiles.title: Application to Export Independent Motion Pictures to Japan

subfiles.about: An application setting forth Transpacific Film Corporation's corporate organization, assets, and catalog in support of exhibition rights in Japan and Korea.
subfiles.summary: Transpacific Film Corporation presents its corporate background, assets, and film inventory, formally applying for licenses to distribute independent American films in occupied Japan and Korea.
subfiles.title: Application to Exhibit Motion Pictures in Japan and Korea

subfiles.about: A letter informing Transpacific Film Corporation that its application was submitted to SCAP, whose decision will be communicated by the War Department.
subfiles.summary: Informs Transpacific Film Corporation that SCAP is reviewing its application and the War Department will communicate the decision.
subfiles.title: Reply to Transpacific Film Corporation on Film Export Application

subfiles.about: An internal office note indicating that no action is required from the Far Eastern Branch concerning the film export application.
subfiles.summary: Internal note agreeing that no action is required from the Far Eastern Branch at this time.
subfiles.title: Internal Note Regarding Transpacific Film Corporation Application

subfiles.about: A letter enclosing for Senator Connally's information a copy of the State Department's reply to Transpacific Film Corporation.
subfiles.summary: Transmits to Senator Connally a copy of the Department's reply to Transpacific Film Corporation regarding film exports.
subfiles.title: Reply to Senator Connally Concerning Transpacific Film Corporation

subfiles.about: A routing slip requesting action on Thomas Betsuin's inquiry concerning the importation of Japanese motion pictures.
subfiles.summary: Routing slip requesting action on Thomas Betsuin's inquiry concerning the importation of Japanese motion picture films.
subfiles.title: Reference Slip on Thomas Betsuin Correspondence Regarding Japanese Films

subfiles.about: An office memorandum referring correspondence concerning Japanese films for appropriate action or referral.
subfiles.summary: Refers correspondence regarding Japanese films to Frank Schuler for response or referral to other interested divisions.
subfiles.title: Office Memo Regarding Correspondence on Japanese Films

subfiles.about: A memorandum transmitting correspondence from Thomas Betsuin regarding the importation of Japanese films to the State Department.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Thomas Betsuin's correspondence regarding Japanese films to the State Department for assistance.
subfiles.title: Transmittal of Thomas Betsuin Correspondence on Japanese Films

subfiles.about: A letter acknowledging Betsuin's inquiry about Japanese film imports and stating that the matter was referred to the State Department.
subfiles.summary: Informs Thomas Betsuin that his inquiry regarding Japanese motion picture film importation was referred to the State Department.
subfiles.title: Letter to Thomas Betsuin Regarding Japanese Film Importation

subfiles.about: A letter asking whether the government or private firms are importing Japanese films into the United States and requesting contact information to rent them.
subfiles.summary: Inquires whether government or private entities are importing Japanese films into the United States and asks about rental terms.
subfiles.title: Inquiry Regarding Importation and Rental of Japanese Films

subfiles.about: A letter advising Betsuin that Japanese films may soon be available for export and directing him to SCAP's Foreign Trade Division.
subfiles.summary: Advises Thomas Betsuin that Japanese films may be available for export and directs him to SCAP's Foreign Trade Division.
subfiles.title: Information Regarding Export of Japanese Motion Picture Films

subfiles.about: A telegram summarizing a Soviet press article alleging that Hollywood and the Central Motion Picture Exchange are monopolizing Japan's film market.
subfiles.summary: Reports Soviet press charges that Hollywood and the Central Motion Picture Exchange are monopolizing Japan's film market under democratization.
subfiles.title: Telegram on Soviet Press Criticism of Hollywood Activities in Japan

subfiles.about: A letter acknowledging Carlisle's proposal to produce short motion picture films in Japan and stating that government agencies are considering the matter.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges Robert Carlisle's proposal to produce short films in Japan and states that government agencies are actively considering it.
subfiles.title: Acknowledgment Regarding Proposed Film Production in Japan

subfiles.about: A diplomatic despatch transmitting Soviet protests against SCAP quotas on Soviet film imports and SCAP's rebuttal based on prewar trade patterns.
subfiles.summary: Sebald transmits Soviet protests claiming SCAP quotas on Soviet film imports violate Allied equality, along with SCAP's response defending prewar trade criteria.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 504: Entry of Soviet Films Into Japan

subfiles.about: A diplomatic letter demanding the revocation of SCAP quotas on Soviet film imports as an unlawful violation of Allied equality and Far Eastern Commission policy.
subfiles.summary: Major General Kislenko protests SCAP restrictions on Soviet film imports as illegal and discriminatory under Far Eastern Commission policy, demanding their revocation.
subfiles.title: Soviet Protest Against Restrictions on Entry of Soviet Films into Japan

subfiles.about: A memorandum defending SCAP's film quota policy under Circular 12 based on prewar trade patterns and requesting documentation of 1935 import claims.
subfiles.summary: SCAP defends film import quotas under Circular 12 based on prewar trade patterns, requesting documentation of alleged 1935 imports.
subfiles.title: Memorandum Defending SCAP Policy on Entry of Soviet Films into Japan
subfiles.to: Acting Soviet Member, Allied Council for Japan

subfiles.about: A telegram reporting statistical data on 35mm movie theaters, total seating capacity, and the proportion of American feature film releases in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Reports Japan has 2,157 35mm theaters seating 1,223,914, with American features comprising 30.7 percent of releases.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 86 on Japanese Motion Picture Theaters and US Feature Releases
